newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Debonair to nearly double air fleet.
newsitem.headline: Debonair to nearly double air fleet.

text.p: Cut-price airline Debonair, a newcomer to the EASDAQ stock market, said on Monday it had signed a letter of intent to lease five more aircraft, taking its fleet to 12 planes.
The airline, which said it planned to invest $12 million over the 12 months to expand operations, will lease five BAe146 aircraft, bringing them into service over the next year.
Debonair, which already operates 11 routes, said the additions to its fleet would raise seat availability by 71 percent and allow it to consider new destinations.

"As the first airline to successfully go public after only a year of operation we wish to continue our expansion and take advantage of deregulation," Chairman and Chief Executive Franco Mancassola said in a statement issued in Brussels.
"Passenger demand has been increasing rapidly over the last year and has encouraged us to make this large commitment to an expanded fleet," he added.
Debonair Holdings Plc, which owns Debonair, floated on the EASDAQ growth stocks market on Friday, trading at around its issue price of 450p after finding support from institutional buyers.
The airline has seen its passenger numbers grow from 3,000 in its first month of operation a year ago to over 50,000 in May 1997.
It said said before its flotation it planned to establish itself as a low fare, "home-based" airline in many European destinations.
